subject: Re: Data deletion walkthrough — logs, backups, prompts, and keystore retention
messages:
From: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@healthcorps.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-07-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Data deletion walkthrough — logs, backups, prompts, keystore

Hi Ben,

Thanks for taking this. As part of HealthCorps' SCC/DPA review we need a concise walkthrough of how Redwood handles deletion for the following data types: request/ingest logs (including request metadata and token-level traces), model prompts/inputs and conversation context, persistent backups and snapshots (object-store and block snapshots), and encryption keystores (KMS/HSM key lifecycle).

Specifically can you confirm: 
- Default retention windows for each type and whether customer-configurable;
- How deletion is applied (logical delete vs physical purge) and how long until data is irrecoverable;
- Behavior for backups & immutable snapshots: are deleted objects retained in snapshots and for how long;
- Prompt retention policy (are prompts ever stored beyond short-term caches/evals);
- Key management: what happens to encryption keys for deleted data (rotation, revocation, retention of revoked keys for audit);
- Evidence we can request to prove deletion happened (S3 object manifest with delete markers, snapshot index invalidation, audit log entries, or signed attestations);

We also need a preferred contact (technical + legal) and any standard artifacts you can share (SOC 2 Type II, retention matrix, sample deletion manifest). Our PO will expect confirmation in the next 48 hours.

Thanks,
Alice Nguyen
Senior Security Engineer — HealthCorps
security+evidence@healthcorps.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@healthcorps.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-07-19T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Data deletion walkthrough — logs, backups, prompts, keystore

Hi Alice — thank you for the clear list. High-level answers below, and I'm attaching a compact retention matrix and our most recent SOC 2 Type II report for HealthCorps' review. Laura (DPO) and Rishi (Security Compliance) are looped for any legal/technical deep-dive.

Quick summary: 
- Request logs (ingest metadata): default 45 days, configurable per-account up to 365 days on enterprise plans. Logical deletion occurs immediately; physical purge of objects and index entries occurs as background job within the configured TTL window and is auditable.
- Backups & snapshots: immutable daily snapshots retained for 365 days by default for Hosted customers. Soft-delete window of 30 days for snapshot restores; after 30 days snapshot indices are invalidated and object versions are eligible for garbage collection following retention expiry.
- Prompts & conversational inputs: default ephemeral retention — cached in-memory for 24 hours and logged to secure audit storage for 7 days for debugging unless the customer opts-in to longer retention. We do not retain raw prompts beyond the configured policy unless explicit eval/labeling is requested.
- Keystore (KMS/HSM): keys are rotated per policy (90-day rotation). Revoked keys are retained in audit form for 30 days to support in-flight verification and then the key material is wiped in accordance with our crypto-hardware vendor procedures.
- Evidence: we can produce a retention matrix (attached), a signed deletion manifest for object-store deletions (sample available), and audit-log slices showing deletion events. SOC2 report attached; for SCC-specific evidence we can provide a scoped export and a signed attestation.

Action items: 
1) Laura and Rishi to confirm wording for DPA/SCCs footprint and provide any HIPAA-specific constraints.
2) We'll generate a per-account deletion manifest sample and a short playbook describing how to request a deletion proof.

Attached: backup-retention-matrix-2027.xlsx; soc2-type2-2027.pdf

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Lead — Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai | +1 415 555 0198

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@healthcorps.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Data deletion walkthrough — logs, backups, prompts, keystore

Alice / Ben — adding a few compliance clarifications from the DPO side so HealthCorps has explicit language to include in the DPA: 

- Default retention windows (configurable at account level): logs = 45 days (enterprise option 365), snapshots (immutable) = 365 days, snapshot soft-delete (recoverable) = 30 days, prompt-level logs (raw inputs) = 7 days, ephemeral cache = 24 hours. Those are defaults; we can scope shorter limits for regulated customers (e.g., HIPAA customers can elect 30-day snapshot retention at contract signature).
- Deletion semantics: We employ a two-phase deletion: logical delete (immediate) which removes metadata pointers and prevents access; physical purge is executed by a scheduled background job that removes object versions and expunges index entries. Physical purge timing is within the configured retention window; once the purge job completes the records are considered irrecoverable.
- Backups & legal hold: Immutable backup snapshots are retained even if the primary object is deleted until snapshot retention expires or legal hold is removed. For customers that require a legal hold we can retain snapshots beyond default retention and provide a ledger entry marking the hold start/end.
- Keystore audit: KMS/HSM providers keep non-reconstructable audit records for 30 days post-revocation; key material destruction follows vendor-certified wipe routines. We can provide rotation logs and signed key-revocation attestations on request.
- Evidence package: the retention matrix (attached) + deletion-manifest (object ids, delete markers, timestamps) + audit-log slices (signed) are the standard package. If HealthCorps needs an encrypted bundle or notarized attestation we can coordinate with legal.

Please confirm whether HealthCorps wants the standard package or a HIPAA-scoped package (which includes additional log granularity and retention shortfall options).

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Data Protection Officer — Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Alice — attaching the matrix and SOC 2 as promised and summarizing the evidence bundle we'll produce upon request: 

1) Retention matrix (attached) — canonical policy table per data type and per plan.
2) Deletion manifest (sample) — CSV of object ids, delete markers, timestamps, and the background job run id. This is what we deliver when a customer requests proof of deletion.
3) Audit-log slice — signed JSON with event ids for the deletion events.
4) Snapshot ledger entry — index entries showing snapshot creation + invalidation times.

Links: https://drive.redwood.ai/records/HC-RETENTION-EVIDENCE-2027 (contains a zip: retention-matrix + sample-manifest + signed-audit-slice).
